chunks.content: 96 The Hidden LOI Clause That Could Slash Your Purchase Price Hi Sara, Let’s play a quick game of “Which Offer Would You Choose?” You’re selling your accounting practice. Two buyers show up: Buyer A offers $3M Buyer B offers $2.9M Easy choice, right? Spoiler: Buyer A’s offer might not actually be $3M. Tucked halfway through their letter of intent is this quiet little clause: “Closing cash to be reduced by normalized working capital.” Translation: That $3M could quickly drop by $200K, $300K, or more, once adjustments are made. Meanwhile, Buyer B? No deduction. Their “lower” offer might actually leave you with more money at the end of the day. This kind of clause catches a lot of sellers off guard. It sounds reasonable, and it is reasonable in the right context. But when it’s not well understood, or not negotiated properly, it can tank your bottom line faster than tax season. So if you’re reviewing multiple LOIs, remember: ✔️ Don’t judge by top-line price alone ✔️ Think beyond the closing table ✔️ Ask hard questions Want more deep dives into LOI terms, hidden pitfalls, and ways to protect your exit?
